findings.title: Public `findMany` removed without updating callers
findings.body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany()` was the only data-fetching entry point and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which merely returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No other files in this PR were updated, so any existing consumer calling `service.findMany({...})` will now fail to compile / throw at runtime. Either keep a `findMany` implemented on top of `$queryRaw`, or update all call sites in the same change.

findings.title: Widened constructor options type loses discriminated-union safety
findings.body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `scope` is a plain union and `teamId` is optional. Previously the discriminated union forced `teamId` to be present for `scope: "team"`. Now `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` type-checks, zod parsing fails silently, `this.options` becomes null, and every query degrades to `1=0` (empty results) with no error surfaced — a hard-to-diagnose data bug.

findings.title: Returned SQL fragments are not self-parenthesized, risking operator-precedence bugs
findings.body: `buildFilterConditions`, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` can return top-level `OR`/`AND` expressions without surrounding parentheses (e.g. `"eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1`, or `(...) OR (...)` for team/org scope). `getBaseConditions` happens to wrap them, but `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` are public and documented as usable directly (the test interpolates conditions into `WHERE ${...}`). Any caller combining them with `AND` will get wrong, potentially authorization-bypassing results. Wrap each returned fragment in parentheses.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions mask an unreachable fallback
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null/undefined, and objects are always truthy), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This hides the intent: if auth conditions were ever intended to be optional, the fail-closed fallback would never trigger. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter, or make the types reflect reality.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely. The caching logic still exists in the service (including the subtle `=== undefined` check that allows caching a `null` filter result), so this behaviour is now untested and regressions (e.g. re-querying memberships on every call) would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Raw-query test asserts exact row shape that may not match driver output
findings.body: `prisma.$queryRaw<{id:number}[]>` returns values with runtime types from the driver; if `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized.id` maps to a 64-bit integer the value comes back as `BigInt`, and `toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])` (a `number`) would fail. The PR description states the tests were never executed, so this assertion needs to be verified against an actual run.
